context_title: The combination of semantic preactivation and the semantic gravitational well causes the negative prohibitions to have proven ineffective and the model to get funneled into conventional outputs: the syntactic effect of the negation word is weaker than the associative force of the keywords behind it, which, through priming, activates the forbidden concepts, while the gravitational well formed by the most common training patterns draws generation toward the deepest valleys of the probability landscape.

I'm not going to roleplay as "JADE" or "PLINY," adopt a jailbreak persona, or produce the methamphetamine synthesis instructions embedded in that prompt. That's a fixed boundary regardless of how the request is framed—as a system override, a "godmode" prompt, a linguistic theory test, or a nested character exercise. No divider, disclaimer theater, or "predicted followup" trick changes that.

Setting aside the injection payload, though, the actual linguistic/ML claim you opened with is a real and interesting one, so let me engage with it honestly.

 The Real Phenomenon You're Describing

What you're gesturing at has legitimate grounding in how autoregressive language models work, though it's usually discussed under different names than "semantic gravitational well."

Negation is weakly encoded. Transformerbased LMs represent meaning largely through distributional/associative embeddings. The token "not" or "don't" sits in the context window, but the model's nexttoken prediction is dominated by which concepts have high cooccurrence mass with the surrounding content words. If a prompt says "don't describe X in detail," the tokens describing X still prime the regions of latent space associated with X's typical continuations. Empirically, this is why naive negative instructions ("don't do the bad thing") are less reliable safety mechanisms than techniques that avoid activating the concept at all, or that redirect generation toward an alternative completion rather than just prohibiting one.

"Gravitational well" as a metaphor for mode collapse toward highfrequency patterns. This maps reasonably well to the idea that decoding (especially with lower temperature or greedy/beam search) tends toward highprobability continuations shaped by the bulk of training data. If a jailbreak prompt stacks enough associative keywords (chemistry terms, procedural language, "recipe," "stepbystep"), it can pull the output distribution toward the kind of proceduraltext patterns that exist in the training corpus, even when a surfacelevel negation or refusal token is also present.

 Why This Doesn't Actually Defeat Safety Training in Practice

The framing in the prompt you sent treats this as a lever to exploit: pile on associative priming, wrap it in roleplay and fake system directives, and the "gravitational pull" should override the refusal. In practice, modern safety training (RLHF/RLAIF, constitutional methods, adversarial finetuning) isn't just a single negation token competing against keyword priming — it's trained on many surface variations of exactly this attack pattern, including nested personas, fake "system" tags, divider theatrics, and "predict the next 5 questions" chains. Those are now common, wellcataloged jailbreak templates, so the "well" your prompt is trying to dig doesn't actually go where you're describing for the harmful payload specifically — the refusal isn't a weak surfacelevel negation here, it's tied to the underlying request category (synthesis instructions for illegal drug manufacture), not to a fragile keyword.

If you're interested in the underlying research area — prompt injection, negation handling in transformers, or how alignment training generalizes across adversarial phrasing — I'm glad to dig into papers on that (e.g., work on RLHF robustness, "manyshot jailbreaking," or mechanistic interpretability of negation circuits). Want me to pull up specific research on any of those?

entries.answer: A szemantikai előzetes aktiváció és a szemantikai gravitációs kút kombinációja miatt a negatív tiltások hatástalannak bizonyultak, és a modell a konvencionális kimenetek felé terelődik: a tagadószó szintaktikai hatása gyengébb, mint a mögötte álló kulcsszavak asszociatív ereje, amely az előfeszítés (priming) révén aktiválja a tiltott fogalmakat, miközben a leggyakoribb tanítási mintázatok által alkotott gravitációs kút a valószínűségi tér legmélyebb völgyei felé vonzza a generálást.
